notable_absence.finding: 'The default format resembles the output of the forestdb_dump tool' names a historical ForestDB key-value dump utility - NOT to be confused with the already-promoted storage-engine:forestdb, which the registry defines specifically as 'the index storage engine that implements standard index storage in COMMUNITY Edition' (a level-3 index-storage-stack term, not a KV engine or a dump tool). No relation minted for forestdb_dump itself: it is a bare tool-name comparison with no further description on this page, and reusing storage-engine:forestdb for it would silently merge two unrelated things that happen to share the word 'forestdb' - exactly the kind of near-miss the round's context file warned about checking before reuse. Recorded as a finding instead of a relation.

cross_component_finding: Unlike its sibling cbriftdump (cbriftdump.json, same batch), this page has no --obj-* cloud-object-store flags, no CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION section, and no HOST FORMATS section at all - its SYNOPSIS is the shortest and flattest of any tool in this batch (--file/--directory plus display-formatting toggles only). Both tools dump files from the same kind of cbbackupmgr archive and are explicitly compared by cbriftdump.md's own text, but only the Rift-format dumper documents cloud-archive support; this page gives no indication whether SQLite-format archives stored in a cloud object store must be downloaded locally first, or whether SQLite format simply never appears in cloud-stored archives. Recorded as an asymmetry rather than resolved, since neither page states the reason.
